fixes.title: Validate product identity before serving compatibility
fixes.problem: Exact Sandwich Starters and Cookie Dough candidates were available but ignored. Brisket was absent and a different sandwich was accepted. “Zuppa” was treated as soup.
fixes.change: Represent brand, restaurant, product, flavor, preparation and size as explicit constraints. Screen both library and search candidates against contradictions before ranking unit convenience. Normalize known speech aliases from verified personal vocabulary. Require a reasoned fallback if no identity-compatible candidate exists; a calorie agreement alone cannot validate identity.
fixes.existing: Adapt the current candidate ranker, personal vocabulary, trusted memory and two-pass search. No new service or model required.
fixes.validation: Replay exact failed words plus held-out brands/flavors; exact product should win even when a generic library food has easier units. Brisket may remain estimated but must never become Honey Bacon Club or add soup.
fixes.efficiency: Filter candidates cheaply before model calls; cache only with complete identity/variant keys. Avoid unconditional stronger-model retry.
fixes.confidence: High for identity preservation; exact missing menu nutrition remains uncertain.

fixes.title: Make serving basis explicit and validate bridges
fixes.problem: A generic serving became 1/21 of a snack; unspecified bread became four buns; packed cans and box fractions depend on guessed yield. Halo Top row mixes per-serving and per-pint numbers.
fixes.change: Keep consumed quantity, database serving quantity, servings per package, drained yield, and nutrient basis separate. A serving cannot mean one piece without evidence. Permit exact unit arithmetic first; attach evidence/estimated status to count-to-mass or package bridges. Reject unsupported whole-item equivalences and conflicting per-serving/per-container rows.
fixes.existing: Extend current deterministic conversion and V9 bridge fields; use existing barcode/label route for package facts.
fixes.validation: 90-calorie snack stays 90; one bun stays one bun; 75% box uses actual package count; five Halo Top label servings use ~500 kcal with correctly based protein. Include 1/2, 1/3, 70%, 75% and count servings.
fixes.efficiency: No model call for grams↔ounces, identical counts, or known package fractions. Ask/flag only missing conversions that materially affect totals.
fixes.confidence: High for refusing unsupported arithmetic; unresolved package dimensions still need evidence.

fixes.title: Apply stated nutrients independently and by scope
fixes.problem: Miso Crunch 4×170 became 170; calorie-only burrito, rice and snacks received zero protein; guessed wrap calories became authoritative.
fixes.change: Store each nutrient as value + basis + confidence (per serving, per container, total eaten). Preserve user constraints only for the nutrients actually supplied. Resolve other nutrients using an identity-compatible source or leave unknown. Treat “I think / maybe / somewhere” as uncertain, not a verified label. Resolve contradictory totals explicitly.
fixes.existing: The current uncommitted code already separates nutrients and fixes the Miso 680-total case; 78 targeted tests pass. Preserve that work and validate full route before deployment. Hedged certainty remains unmodeled in the parser helper.
fixes.validation: Exact Miso transcript →680 kcal and compatible protein; 500-calorie burrito retains ~22 g if matching label; 250-calorie rice gets plausible nonzero protein; calorie-only speech never creates a false zero.
fixes.efficiency: Reuse the already selected source to fill missing nutrients. Bypass AI only when all required nutrients and their basis are known.
fixes.confidence: High for deterministic scope and missing-value fixes.

fixes.change: Add a percent/fraction-of-container parser before label multiplication; use printed per-container totals when available. With the retained pot-pie label, 0.7×820=574 kcal and 0.7×36=25.2 g protein.

Keep package label serving, consumed amount and UI increment separate. Normalize library measurement units without losing density or flavor.

Keep audio only with an explicit retention choice. Redact and cap stored payloads.

limitations: Window is 30 local diary dates: October 13–November 11, 2026 inclusive. Seven October 12 records appear only in a boundary appendix. Diary date is used, not necessarily the recording’s timestamp.

92 recoverable exact-text/day utterance groups are scored: 91 present in current diary plus one deleted attempt recovered from backups. No persistent capture ID exists, so identical repeated recordings on the same day cannot always be distinguished.

Raw audio is not retained in these records. Transcription fidelity cannot be scored; the saved transcript is the starting point. Voice and typed text are not reliably distinguishable. Empty-audio failure is counted separately.

This is not proof that all utterances ever attempted in the month were recovered. Daily/recent backups are incomplete; unsaved/deleted attempts can be missing entirely. Only Alexander’s profile was read for meal content.

Stage scores concern retained evidence. Search results are cached snapshots and do not reveal the exact original HTTP query, cache hit, or every retry. Library references resolve against current definitions unless a historical definition is independently available.
Raw pass candidate indexes are batch-local; final stored indexes refer to the full result list. Do not compare the numbers directly without the missing batch mapping.
Current and first automatic results are not equivalent. Snapshot transitions are observations, not actor-attributed correction events. The Halo Top amount change cannot be assigned to AI or user.

A 2 means reasonable agreement, not a verified nutrition label. Generic fruits/vegetables, cooked/raw state, oils, package sizes and flavor versions remain assumptions where unstated. A 1 is not a confirmed failure.

No production diary, library, prompt or deployment was changed. Local probes used existing functions without external model calls. Existing uncommitted product changes were left untouched. Recommendations have not been benchmarked end-to-end.
